title: Travel app Hopper to pay $35M in FTC settlement over ‘unfairly’ charging hidden fees
slides: Hopper promised cheap flights. Did it hide costs?
The FTC says it added fees after booking started.
The settlement is $35M—but not for refunds.
You now have the right to see all fees upfront.
Before booking, check for buried surcharges first.
thread_text:
1. Did you really save?

Hopper promised cheap flights but hid fees until after booking, costing users millions.

2. FTC catches the trap.

The Federal Trade Commission says Hopper tacked on undisclosed fees after you already committed.

3. $35M changes nothing.

The settlement money goes to the government, not to the customers who overpaid.

4. Now you can see everything.

A new rule forces Hopper to show you the full price before you click confirm.

5. Check for buried costs first.

Before your next booking, scroll to the bottom of the price breakdown. Have you ever missed a hidden fee?

carousel_slides.hook: The price you saw wasn't real.
carousel_slides.description: Hopper lured users with low fares, then secretly added fees after booking started. Millions overpaid before anyone noticed.
The Federal Trade Commission found Hopper unfairly tacked on charges after users committed. The trap is now public.
The settlement money won't refund overcharged customers. It flows to the Treasury, not to those who were cheated.
A new rule requires Hopper to show you all fees before you click confirm. No more surprises after checkout.

carousel_slides.hook: Save this before your next booking.
carousel_slides.description: Scroll to the bottom of any Hopper price breakdown and look for buried surcharges before you pay.
